chapter_seo_title: Chapter 400: Reinforcements – Blind Chen Returns with a Bagua Mirror Massacre
chapter_meta_description: Lu Xiucai survives a monk-skin monster, but Blind Chen’s Bagua mirror kills the grave-robber crew. A philosophical bombshell about “Cultivating the True vs. False” rewrites the rules of reality.
og_title: Dao Twisted World Ch. 400: Blind Chen’s Bagua Massacre & the True/False Bomb
og_description: A blind fortune teller reduces an entire grave-robbing crew to red slime, and the Zuowandao’s core secret is finally revealed.
twitter_description: Lu Xiucai survives a stitched-skin monster, then Blind Chen turns a gang into puddles. Also: the biggest lore bomb yet—Cultivate the True vs. False.

lore_anchors.definition: A Taoist ritual tool used for exorcism, reflection of evil, and directional feng shui adjustment; in this chapter, it is weaponized to lethal effect.
The highest-ranked inner circle of the Zuowandao; their appearance signals an escalation in the enemy's threat level.
Ritual burn scars on a monk's scalp, marking ordination; the presence of these on the skin confirms its origin as a monk’s scalp.
A government-sponsored supernormal law enforcement body believed to be under the imperial board of war; they hunt rogue practitioners and manage supernatural disasters.
A euphemism for a professional tomb robber, a low-class trade often associated with the danger of unearthing cursed artifacts.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the “monk-skin” in this chapter?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It’s a stitched-together piece of human skin made from multiple monk scalps, complete with ritual burn scars (jieba) and fake Sanskrit writing. It’s a classic folk-horror cursed artifact that grants its wearer unnatural stretching abilities.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Blind Chen kill everyone with the Bagua mirror?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Blind Chen is an itinerant ritualist with a grudge; in the Dao-Twisted World, any ritual tool in the wrong (or right) hands can be weaponized. He’s not a hero—he’s a survivor who treats his skills as tools for personal gain.

It’s the Zuowandao’s core philosophy: the power to “cultivate falsehood into reality.” While generic xianxia cultivators seek enlightenment (zhen, truth), the Zuowandao believe they can make lies real through sheer stubborn faith. This is the secret behind their illusions and reality-warping tricks.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is Lu Xiucai a threat now?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Not yet. He survives this encounter through luck and a timely rescue, but it’s the first time he’s faced real supernatural horror. His later cockiness and growing greed are a warning sign, not a power spike.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why do the grave-robbers fear the Supervisory Heavenly Office?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The Office is a government-sanctioned supernormal police force with almost unlimited authority over supernatural crimes. Grave-robbers who unearth cursed artifacts are exactly the kind of illegal practitioners the Office would summarily execute.
